newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police detain three in kidnap investigation.
newsitem.headline: German police detain three in kidnap investigation.

text.p: Police hunting for kidnapped German multi-millionaire Jakub Fiszmann detained two men and a woman on Wednesday and searched buildings and apartments in the Frankfurt area, prosecutors said.

Rainer Schilling, the spokesman for the Frankfurt prosecutor's office, declined to give any more details about the three or about what had been found in the searches. He said more information would be given at a late afternoon news confernence.
Asked if Fiszmann was still alive, he replied: "There is still no information one way or another."
The searches took place in Frankfurt, Wiesbaden and Mainz, the spokesman said.
Fiszmann, a 40-year old businessman and member of one of Germany's richest families, was abducted outside his Frankfurt office on October 1.
The only contact with Fiszmann since then has been a phone call he made to a contact, believed to be his girlfriend, saying he that he was being kept in a cellar.
Fiszmann's brother Georg paid a four million mark ransom ($2.6 million) on October 10 for his release, but his kidnappers failed to free him as promised the following day.
Police said on Tuesday they believed Fiszmann was still alive, following a statement from the kidnappers that the victim had enough provisions to survive for four weeks.

The police also believe that Fiszmann has been abducted by a German criminal gang, following a telephone message in a German accent from the kidnappers, and not by the Russian mafia or international terrorists as some media had speculated.
The Fiszmann family on Monday offered a one millon mark reward for information and police hoped the offer would lead to clues to help free the missing multi-millionaire.
Since then the police have combed the countryside around Frankfurt looking for Fiszmann. Earlier this week, 25 police officers searched a former U.S. army arms depot.
Searchers used helicopters and tracker dogs to comb the area after an anonymous telephone caller said cars police believe were connected with the kidnap had been seen in the area.
Police have also been monitoring the sale of mediaction which Fiszmann needs to treat acute food allergies.
Fiszmann runs a property and electronics company in Frankfurt and is also known locally for financing the production of the musical "Tommy" in Offenbach near Frankfurt.
Police believe that his abductors may be part of the same gang who unsuccessfully tried to extort money during an aborted kidnap of Fiszmann's nephew in 1991.
It appears Fiszmann tried to fight off his kidnappers as his broken wristwatch and small amounts of blood were found in a white van used in the abduction and later recovered by police.
